title: Perpendicular bisectors and Voronoi diagrams
summary: Equations of perpendicular bisectors and how they build Voronoi diagrams, used for nearest-neighbour interpolation and the “toxic waste dump” problem.

keyterms.definition: ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2), the point halfway between two points.
The line through the midpoint of AB at right angles to AB; every point on it is equidistant from A and B.
A division of the plane into cells, each holding the points closest to one site.
One of the given points around which a Voronoi cell is built.
The region of all points closer to one site than to any other.
A boundary between two neighbouring cells; part of a perpendicular bisector.
A point where three or more edges meet; equidistant from three or more sites.
Estimating a value at a point using the value at the site whose cell contains it.
Finding the point in a region furthest from every site; it lies at a Voronoi vertex or on the boundary.

questions.explanation: Average the coordinates: ((2 + 8)/2, (4 + 10)/2).

questions.prompt: Find the perpendicular bisector of (2, 4) and (8, 10).
questions.explanation: AB has gradient 1, so the bisector has gradient −1 through (5, 7): y = −x + 12.

questions.statement: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is the same distance from A and from B.
questions.explanation: This is why bisectors form the boundaries of Voronoi cells.

questions.text: The perpendicular bisector of AB passes through the ___ of AB.
questions.explanation: It bisects (halves) AB at right angles.

questions.prompt: Find the perpendicular bisector of (0, 0) and (6, 0).
questions.explanation: AB is horizontal, so the bisector is the vertical line through (3, 0).

questions.statement: The perpendicular bisector of AB has the same gradient as AB.
questions.explanation: Its gradient is the negative reciprocal of AB’s gradient.

questions.prompt: A(1, 1) and B(5, 3). Find the gradient of the perpendicular bisector of AB.
questions.explanation: AB has gradient 2/4 = 0.5; the negative reciprocal is −2.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: the same distance from two or more points

questions.explanation: Together these describe a perpendicular bisector.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for finding a perpendicular bisector in order.
items: Substitute the midpoint into y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)
questions.explanation: Midpoint and perpendicular gradient fix the line.

questions.text: The perpendicular bisector of (1, 3) and (1, 9) is y = ___.
questions.explanation: AB is vertical, so the bisector is horizontal through the midpoint (1, 6).

questions.text: Each region of a Voronoi diagram is called a ___.
questions.explanation: Each cell surrounds one site.

questions.statement: Every point inside a cell is closer to that cell’s site than to any other site.
questions.explanation: That is the defining property of a Voronoi cell.

questions.prompt: The edges of a Voronoi diagram lie on:
questions.explanation: Points on an edge are equidistant from the two sites either side.

questions.prompt: A Voronoi vertex is equidistant from:
questions.explanation: It lies on edges between three or more cells.

questions.prompt: A village lies in the cell of weather station A, which recorded 40 mm of rain. Nearest neighbour interpolation estimates the village’s rainfall as:
options: the value at the nearest vertex
questions.explanation: The estimate is the value of the site whose cell contains the point.

questions.statement: In the toxic waste dump problem, the best location is at a Voronoi vertex or on the boundary of the region.
questions.explanation: These are the candidates for being furthest from all sites.

questions.prompt: When a new site is added to a Voronoi diagram:
options: only the cells next to the new site change
questions.explanation: The new cell takes area only from neighbouring cells.

questions.prompt: Match each Voronoi term to its meaning.

pairs.right: the given point a cell is built around
point where three or more edges meet
region of points nearest one site

questions.explanation: Learn these words: questions use them precisely.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for adding a site to a Voronoi diagram in order.
items: Draw perpendicular bisectors between the new site and neighbouring sites
Find where these bisectors meet existing edges
Remove edge segments now inside the new cell
questions.explanation: The new cell is bounded by the new bisectors.

questions.prompt: Sites are at A(0, 0), B(4, 0) and C(0, 6). Find the Voronoi vertex.
questions.explanation: It lies on x = 2 (bisector of AB) and y = 3 (bisector of AC), so (2, 3).
